title: Validation and evaluation of the EUREKA AI system for real-time support in surgery based on a European patient cohort
summary:
Background:
Technological progress has been remarkable in surgery especially regarding optics and robotics. Recent surgical devices can effectively support surgeon's eyes and hands through advanced endoscopes and improved surgical platforms (i.e., surgical robots). However, adverse events during surgical procedures remain an unresolved critical issue. Approximately 30% of adverse events during surgical procedures are related to cognition. The causes of decreased cognitive ability and performance of surgeons include:
a)	Fatigue due to long working hours and/or long operative time
b)	Decreased concentration and attention affected by physical and mental stress
c)	Inexperience in anatomical knowledge and technical skills.
Recognizing that there are many adverse events due to the decline in cognitive ability and performance in surgical operations, Anaut Inc. (Anaut) has focused on the development and use of an artificial intelligence (“AI”, EUREKA) system that detects anatomical structures and events (e.g., connective tissue, nerves, blood vessels, blood, surgical devices, etc.) during surgery.

Aim:
 Existing preclinical testing and results from Japan have demonstrated that EUREKA can detect difficult-to-discern anatomical structures at a level convincing to expert surgeons. However, a knowledge gap remains regarding the system's performance in the European population. This clinical investigation aims to address this gap by evaluating the system's efficacy in colorectal, liver, pancreatic or upper gastrointestinal tract procedures within a European context. 
The aim is to establish AI that is suitable for European patients by evaluating its effectiveness against surgical data from European patients, improving the AI if any issues are identified, and then reevaluating the effectiveness of the improved AI. To achieve this, it is necessary to evaluate the AI using surgical videos from Europe under various conditions, such as BMI and race.
conditions: Elective operations of the following entities: colorectal surgery, operation of the upper GI tract, liver surgery, pancreatic surgery

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of video recordings of surgical procedures performed on prospectively enrolled patients with indications for elective, minimally invasive visceral surgery. The EUREKA AI system, which recognises anatomical structures, is used for this purpose.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 and ≤ 50 kg/m2
Indication for minimally invasive surgery
Exclusion criteria:
ASA ≥ 4
Pregnant or breastfeeding patients
Mental impairment that prevent recognition of nature, kind and extent of the trial
